fields.title: Five criteria, two layers. Not a vibe check.
fields.subtitle: The Pitch by Deel publishes exactly what it scores for. Most competitions do not.

fields.subLabel: The Pitch by Deel scores against, published in full
fields.body: Product strength, market opportunity, team capability, traction, scalability. Each one a named bar, not a general impression.
fields.sourceLine: The Pitch by Deel product-information document, 2026

fields.headline: Two layers means two filters, not one opinion
fields.body: AI analysis runs first. Expert judges run second. The same five criteria govern both passes, so the score is consistent rather than one panel's gut call.

fields.kicker: the cost of one agent doing everything
fields.headline: One LLM call for all tasks cuts corners on the facts that decide eligibility
fields.body: Discovery, validation, scoring and drafting in a single prompt means no step can be verified independently.

fields.headline: Scoring and validation belong to scripts. Drafting belongs to agents.
fields.body: Keep deterministic work deterministic. Generative tools are for synthesis, not for auditing the facts that determine whether you qualify.

fields.headline: Specialized agents, small jobs, verifiable results
fields.body: Each agent in the pipeline owns one bounded task. That is what makes the overall system trustworthy rather than opaque.

fields.headline: What a rebuilt workflow actually preserves
